newsitem.title: FRANCE: French credit card group gets OK for Net software.
newsitem.headline: French credit card group gets OK for Net software.

text.p: Groupement des cartes bancaires CB, the association of French Carte Bleue credit card issuers, said on Thursday it had received government approval to use and market its Chip-Secure Electronic Transaction (C-SET) software, which makes credit card transactions on the Internet secure.
Carte Bleue is the most common credit card in France and is part of the Visa group of credit cards internationally.

The association said in a statement that the authorisation, by a regulatory body attached to the office of Prime Minister Alain Juppe which is responsible for the security of information systems, was the first since a law on cryptography, or encoding, was passed in July 1996.

"All credit establishments which are members of the group can now use, distribute or operate this C-SET software in order to allow their clients, and businesses who wish to, to carry out payments on the Internet in total security," it said.
C-SET is an encoding software developed by Groupement des cartes bancaires CB.
It is completely inter-operable with both Visa and Mastercard networks, the association said.
